hits.name: Codie Sanchez
hits.hook: All employees come in 5 levels, choose wisely:
hits.text:
All employees come in 5 levels, choose wisely:

Level 1 - tells you there's a problem
Level 2 - tells you there's a problem and what caused it
Level 3 - tells you there's a problem, what caused it, and options to fix it
Level 4 - tells you there's a problem, what caused it,
hits.draft_en:
Every market vendor tracks their sales at one of 5 levels:

Level 1 - knows whether it felt busy
Level 2 - knows the total at the end of the day
Level 3 - knows the total and which items sold
Level 4 - knows what sold and what it cost to be there (booth fee, gas, hours)
Level 5 - uses all of it to decide which shows to rebook next year

Vendors: which level are you at right now, honestly? And what got you up one?
hits.video_tip: Talking-head, 20-30s: read the five levels as on-screen text that stacks one line at a time, ending on Level 5 highlighted in burnt orange. Close on the question as a caption.

hits.name: Codie Sanchez
hits.hook: The best skill you'll ever learn, how to stay positive even when you have a thousand reasons not to.
hits.text: The best skill you'll ever learn, how to stay positive even when you have a thousand reasons not to.
hits.draft_en:
The most underrated booth skill: greeting the next person like they're the first one of the day, even when the last hour sold nothing.

The shopper walking up has no idea it's been slow.

Vendors: what's your trick for staying "on" through a dead afternoon?
hits.video_tip: Phone on a tripod in an empty aisle, 10s: one line to camera, then cut to a table being straightened. Or skip video and pair with a cream-paper sketch card of the first line.

hits.name: Shopify
hits.hook: The latest Edition is here and it’s all about Shopify’s network
hits.text:
The latest Edition is here and it’s all about Shopify’s network

1B+ products in our catalog
400M+ shoppers using Shop Pay
150+ updates for exponential growth

You do the math https://t.co/06vyv57M53
hits.draft_en:
Three numbers to know before your next holiday market:

1. Break-even: booth fee + gas + the day's supplies, divided by your average sale. That's how many sales before you're making anything.
2. Stock to bring: what sold at your last show this size, plus extra of your top two sellers.
3. Walk-away line: the total that makes this show worth booking again next year.

Write them on a card and tape it under the table.

Vendors: which of the three do you actually know before you load the car?
hits.video_tip: Hands-only overhead, 15-20s: write the three numbers on an index card with a marker, then tape it under a folding table. Captions carry each line; no voiceover needed.
